questions.explanation_html:
Use the relation:﻿Unemployment Rate(UR)=LFPR−WPRLFPR×100{\mathrm{Unemployment~Rate}}\left({\mathrm{UR}}\right)=\frac{\mathrm{LFPR}-{\mathrm{WPR}}}{\mathrm{LFPR}}\times100Unemployment Rate(UR)=LFPRLFPR−WPR​×100﻿Given:

  • LFPR = 50%
  • WPR = 45%

﻿UR=50−4550×100=550×100=10%UR=\frac{50-45}{50}\times100=\frac{5}{50}\times100=10\%UR=5050−45​×100=505​×100=10%﻿Final Answer: 10%


Think of the population in three layers:


1) Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)

  • Who is counted? People who are working OR actively looking for work.
  • Formula:﻿LFPR=LabourForceTotalPopulation×100LFPR=Labour ForceTotal Population×100LFPR=Labour ForceTotal Population×100\text{LFPR} = \frac{\text{Labour Force}}{\text{Total Population}} \times 100LFPR=LabourForceTotalPopulation×100LFPR=Total PopulationLabour Force​×100﻿

👉 It tells you how many people are participating in the job market.


2) Worker Population Ratio (WPR)

  • Who is counted? People who are actually employed.
  • Formula:﻿WPR=EmployedPeopleTotalPopulation×100WPR=Employed PeopleTotal Population×100WPR=Employed PeopleTotal Population×100\text{WPR} = \frac{\text{Employed People}}{\text{Total Population}} \times 100WPR=EmployedPeopleTotalPopulation×100WPR=Total PopulationEmployed People​×100﻿

👉 It tells you how many people are actually working.


3) Unemployment Rate (UR)

  • Who is counted? People who are in the labour force but NOT working.
  • Formula:﻿UR=UnemployedLabourForce×100UR=UnemployedLabour Force×100UR=UnemployedLabour Force×100\text{UR} = \frac{\text{Unemployed}}{\text{Labour Force}} \times 100UR=UnemployedLabourForce×100UR=Labour ForceUnemployed​×100﻿

👉 It tells you how many job-seekers couldn’t find work.


Simple Example

Suppose a village has 100 people:

  • 50 people are working
  • 10 people are looking for jobs
  • 40 people are not interested in working (students, elderly, etc.)

Step-by-step:

  • Labour Force = 50 (working) + 10 (unemployed) = 60
  • LFPR = 60 / 100 × 100 = 60%
  • WPR = 50 / 100 × 100 = 50%
  • Unemployment Rate = 10 / 60 × 100 = 16.67%

Intuition (very important)

  • LFPR → Who is in the game
  • WPR → Who is winning (has a job)
  • Unemployment Rate → Who is trying but losing (jobless)
